author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form prefilled with its current values. The correction updates that visit in place, follows the booking rules, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit holds the new values, the pet has no additional visit, and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a blank description or a date of today or earlier is submitted, then the correction is refused, the form is shown again, and the offending field is named
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused and changes no visit
edge case 4: a refused correction leaves the stored visit unchanged
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-4, NG-5)
any link or button to the correction form on the owner detail page or elsewhere: the owner decided the form is reachable by its URL alone in this request
a confirmation message after a correction: the request does not ask for one
a different validation rule for visits whose date has passed: the request says correction validates like creation
notes: Owner-specified mechanism carried as intake context for system-design-expert: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, reuse template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with its `visit` model attribute, redirect to the owner detail page on success. No prd-autofix records to audit. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions (past-dated visits, confirmation message, entry point); none blocks this slice. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for 2026-10-24-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForInvalidDetails is one data-driven test covering blank description and non-future date.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the Owner aggregate write path (system-design § Contracts invariants: Pet and Visit persist only by cascade from Owner through OwnerRepository) and mirrors the existing edit seam in PetController (GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit). One adjustment is required inside VisitController: its @ModelAttribute("visit") loader (loadPetWithVisit) unconditionally creates a new Visit and adds it to the pet for every handler in the class. On the edit routes it must instead return the pet's existing visit found by identity, or owners.save(owner) cascades a phantom extra visit, which breaks the 'no additional visit' criterion. The suggested form is an optional visitId path variable on the loader. The lookup goes Owner.getPet(petId) then a new Pet.getVisit(Integer id), mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). The non-future-date check is the rule the existing recorded controller deviation names (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog note; system-design § Package Structure). It is not a new rule, so it moves into one private method shared by both POST handlers rather than being duplicated. Basis: grep and Read of VisitController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java and the template; the IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Binding (new entry point POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit): the target is the persisted Visit loaded through the aggregate, behind an allow-list. Add @InitBinder("visit") with setAllowedFields("date", "description") and keep the existing class-wide setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (security-principles § Mass assignment). The visit is never bound whole.
Binding (new entry point GET .../visits/{visitId}/edit): binds nothing; it reads the path identifiers only.

Repository boundary in tests: extend the existing @WebMvcTest fixture's @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub. Reason: OwnerRepository is a JpaRepository whose hand-written double would implement the whole interface, and the class already stubs it (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: tolerated stub, conscious exception). For the in-place criterion, assert the owner passed to save holds the pet's original visit count and the visit with the new values. For refusals, verify save is never called.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Template: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm already posts to the current URL (no th:action) and hides the 'New' heading for a persisted visit. No template change is required. Any label change must reuse an existing message key or add the key to all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002).

patterns.description: existing GET/POST edit pair under an owner: load by identity, redisplay the form on errors, save through OwnerRepository, redirect to the owner
lookup-by-identity shape to mirror for Pet.getVisit(Integer)
ownership refusal by IllegalArgumentException in the model-attribute loader; extend it to a visit not found under the pet

risks.risk: The @ModelAttribute("visit") loader adds a transient Visit to the pet on every request, so a correction saved through the owner cascades an additional visit (system-design § Contracts invariants: cascade from Owner).
risks.mitigation: On edit routes the loader returns the existing visit and adds nothing. A test asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged in the saved graph.

risks.risk: Edge case 3: a visit outside the named pet, or a pet outside the named owner, could be corrected.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only through Owner.getPet(petId) and then Pet.getVisit(visitId). A miss throws IllegalArgumentException before binding, as the existing loader does. The message carries only identifiers (security-principles § Secret disclosure: the error page renders the message).

risks.risk: Edge case 4: a refused correction mutates the stored visit.
risks.mitigation: Binding mutates only the detached in-memory visit (open-in-view is disabled; system-design § Persistence). The error path returns the form without calling save, and a test verifies that save is never called.

risks.risk: Visit correction lookup scales with a pet's visits (system-design § Scale and Load, Visit correction lookup row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear scan, size unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Duplicating the non-future-date check in a second handler adds a fresh controller rule (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).
risks.mitigation: Both POST handlers call one private check, which stays under the existing recorded deviation.

notes: Design-doc writes: § Contracts rows Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now carry REQ-VIS-003, with the VisitController and Pet purposes updated. The invariants paragraph gains the in-place correction statement. § Security Context inputs now name visit identifiers. A new § Scale and Load section holds the visit correction lookup row. docs/adr/README.md index gains the row for 2026-10-24-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, and the 2026-08-08 status column notes the NG-5 amendment, as the prd-entry requested. No architectural ADR: the loader branching is contained in this slice. The product expert authored the non-goal ADRs (2026-10-24 new, 2026-08-08 status line) within its write scope; they are not claimed here. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records. Out of scope per prd-entry: no edit link, no confirmation flash message, no separate rule for past-dated visits.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: docs/system-design.md:90 assigns 'looks one up by identity' to Pet, a seam below the web boundary. The lookup (match on id, skip unsaved visits, null when absent) is exercised only through the @WebMvcTest in VisitControllerTests. `grep -n 'getVisit(' -r src/test` returns no match, so no unit test exists at the Pet seam. A regression in the lookup (wrong id comparison, returning an unsaved visit) would surface only as a distant controller failure. Add a plain unit test of Pet.getVisit: found by id, absent id returns null, an unsaved visit is not returned.

The correction POST sets `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)` and a visit-scoped allowed-fields binder, and docs/system-design.md:179 lists mass assignment via form binding as a threat. No test submits an extra owner field (e.g. lastName) or an id alongside date and description. Removing `binding = false` or `allowVisitFields` would leave every test green. The binding guard on the new route is untested.
findings.fix: Add a test that posts the correction with an extra owner parameter (e.g. lastName) and id=UNKNOWN_ID. Assert the saved owner's last name and the visit's id are unchanged.

findings.description: The outcome is read through an ArgumentCaptor and a chain (getPet(...).getVisits()), where the brief's Assertions section calls for whole-object comparison of the saved state. Compare the whole expected Owner, or at least the whole pet, with a recursive comparison against an expected owner built with the existing factories.
findings.fix: Build the expected owner with createAnOwnerWithPet(createAPetWithVisit(createAVisit(CORRECTED_DATE, CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION))) and compare it to the captured owner with usingRecursiveComparison.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the new `@InitBinder("visit")` allow-list (VisitController.java:58 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");`) stacks on the existing global disallow (VisitController.java:53 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");`), so the visit binder on both the new and the correction routes accepts only the two form fields; the template's hidden `petId` input cannot reach the visit, and the correction handler binds the owner with `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, which is stronger than the new-visit route's bound `Owner`, an existing pattern this change does not extend

Object-level scoping and cross-request state: each correction request re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit from path variables in `loadPetWithVisit`, and `Pet.getVisit` only matches persisted visits within that pet's own collection, so a visitId from another pet or owner throws before any save; the parameterized refusal test asserts `never()).save` for both cases

Validation parity: the correction handler carries `@Valid Visit` and calls the same `rejectDateNotInFuture` helper extracted from the booking handler, so no check was removed or weakened in the refactor

Error disclosure: the new `IllegalArgumentException` message carries only the caller-supplied visit id and the pet id, the same shape as the neighbouring owner/pet not-found messages (VisitController.java:75, PetController.java:70); no credential or internal detail reaches the rendered error page

Persistence side effect: `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11) keeps the loaded entities detached, so a refused correction that mutated the bound visit is never flushed, since no `save` runs on the error path

Output escaping: the reused `pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html` renders visit description and owner/pet values via `th:text`; `grep -rn -F -e 'utext' src/main/resources/templates` returned no match; `__${name}__` preprocessing in `fragments/inputField.html` takes only literal field names, never request text

Surface: two new routes (GET/POST `/owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit`) expose correction of an existing visit's date and description only, consistent with the open-demonstration baseline in docs/security-principles.md; no management exposure change, no new query text, no file or process sinks in the diff

Secrets and supply chain: the diff's added-line sweep for password/secret/token/credential hits only a system-design.md sentence about environment-supplied datasource credentials; build.gradle is unchanged and no dependency scanner is configured (`grep -i dependencycheck build.gradle` empty), so no NVD match ran: resolved runtimeClasspath shows Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Hibernate 7.4.5.Final

blast_radius.note: Two production files in one module (VisitController, Pet), no sensitive paths; the 37 hunks are mostly docs and tests.
